messages:
lina-support: Hey team — customer maria says their CI deploys to prod started failing with 401s from the Redwood API after a token rotation. Can we triage?

maria-customer: Update from the field: our GitHub Actions job that runs `infra/deploy` started failing ~08:23 UTC. The job uses a service account token stored in `REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN`. Example error from the job: 

```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token expired or revoked"}
request-id: rq_01G8X2K7
```

We rotated some org keys last week but I don't think the CI token was part of that rotation. The token was originally created 2025-11-10.

Any quick checks we can run?

sam-devx: Thanks — couple quick questions: 1) is the pipeline using an API key or a service-account token? 2) can you paste the full failing curl (with token redacted)? Also, do you see a `token_type` or `expires_in` anywhere in the secret metadata?

maria-customer: It's a service account token (CI bot). We redacted the token but here's the invocation we run in GH actions: 

```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deploys -d '{"env":"prod","version":"v3.2.1"}' \
  || true
```

We don't have expires_in in our vault entry. I can fetch the service account metadata if that helps.

oliver-oncall: Quick check: try introspecting the token so we can see expiry/iss/claims. If your token was issued before a org-wide revocation it may show a `revoked` flag. Run: 

```
# local (redact token before paste)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SA_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/introspect
```

If that endpoint returns 401 for introspect it means the token isn't valid at all. Also check the request-id from the job against our logs (you posted rq_01G8X2K7). I'll look it up in the log service.

maria-customer: Ran introspect — got 401 there too. Paste from job log: `token expired or revoked`. Our audit shows a manual rotation of some admin API keys on 2026-02-12 (ops rotation), but again the CI token wasn't touched in Vault. Not sure what triggered the revoke.

sam-devx: Two paths here: short-term unblock and long-term fix. Short-term: create a new service-account token scoped only for CI and rotate the secret in GH actions. Long-term: recommend moving away from long-lived static tokens — use OIDC/GitHub Actions or short-lived tokens created by the service account on demand.

On scopes: CI deploys generally only need a tight set of permissions. For our platform I'd recommend at minimum: `deploy:write`, `models:read` (if you pull model manifests), and `logs:write` (so CI can push deploy logs). Avoid anything like `org:admin` or `billing:*`. If you must create a longer-lived token for a third-party runner, restrict it to `ci:invoke` / `deploy:write` and set expiry.

pat-infra: I can create a short-lived token for the service account from the control plane if you want. Example request we support (POST to the service account tokens endpoint) — you can use this to create ephemeral tokens programmatically from a machine that has higher perms: 

```
POST /v1/service_accounts/sa-12345/tokens
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "note": "ci-github-actions",
  "scopes": ["deploy:write","models:read"],
  "expires_in": 86400  # seconds (24h)
}
```

Response returns the token and `expires_at`. For GH Actions, prefer OIDC + short-lived tokens. If you need help wiring that up I can pair.

maria-customer: Ok we created a new token via the endpoint with expires_in=86400 and updated the repo secret. The job passed on the new run — deployment succeeded. Thanks.

lina-support: Great — can you confirm the old token value is revoked? If not, we should revoke it and record the change in your rotation policy. Also please confirm no other infra pieces were relying on the old token.

maria-customer: Confirmed — I revoked the old token via the UI and removed it from Vault. I also searched for occurrences of the token name and nothing else popped up.

sam-devx: FYI for the team: if you must use long-lived tokens (not recommended) set an explicit expiration and scope them narrowly. Recommended policy we should document for customers: default to ephemeral (OIDC) -> if static token required, max 30 days and narrow scopes, rotate automatically. I'll create a short doc snippet in devex.

oliver-oncall: I'll correlate the `rq_01G8X2K7` entry — looks like it did show as `revoked` around 2026-03-08 07:12 UTC in our token service (ops applied a bulk revoke rule for keys created before 2025-12-01). That explains why the token died even though the customer didn't rotate it manually. We should improve our communication for these bulk-revokes.

lina-support: Action items: 1) sam to add a devex note on CI token best practices and example OIDC config; 2) pat to add a one-click control plane flow for creating short-lived SA tokens (we already have API but expose in UI); 3) oliver to add alerting/announcements when org-wide revokes happen (so customers are notified). Maria — flag if you want us to open a follow-up ticket on any of those.

maria-customer: All good, thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: (system) Deployment finished for repo infra at 09:12 UTC, sha=3a7c9f, trigger=github-actions/ci-deploy#72

lina-support: Closing thread — resolved by rotating CI token to scoped, short-lived token and revoking old token. Reopen if it reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
